title: NVIDIA Open-Sources Its Platform for Building Physical AI
summary: NVIDIA published Cosmos, a free open platform containing world models, datasets, and tools for building AI that operates in the physical world — robots, self-driving vehicles, and smart infrastructure.

title: A Free Self-Hosted Alternative to Google's NotebookLM Is Now Available
summary: Open-Notebook replicates what Google NotebookLM does — letting you chat with your own documents and generate audio overviews — but runs entirely on your own hardware with no data sent to Google.

title: GitHub Releases an Official SDK for Embedding Copilot Into Any App
summary: GitHub published a multi-platform SDK that lets developers integrate Copilot Agent — its AI coding assistant — directly into third-party tools and services.

title: A Powerful Free OCR Tool Now Feeds Documents Directly Into AI
summary: PaddleOCR converts PDFs, scanned pages, and images into structured text that AI systems can process — supporting over 100 languages.

title: GitHub Releases a Toolkit for Writing Better Specs Before You Build
summary: GitHub published spec-kit to help teams practice Spec-Driven Development — the approach of writing a clear specification before any code is written.

title: A New AI Research Skill Searches Six Platforms in Parallel
summary: Developer mvanhorn published last30days-skill, a reusable skill for AI agent frameworks that takes any topic, searches Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket, and the general web simultaneously, then synthesizes results into a single grounded summary with contradictions flagged across sources.

title: Your AI Agent Can Now Search Six Platforms — With Zero API Fees
summary: Agent-Reach, a new open-source command-line tool, gives AI agents the ability to read and search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, and XiaoHongShu from a single interface — no platform API subscriptions required.

title: OpenAI Publishes an Official Plugins Repository on GitHub
summary: OpenAI released an official plugins repository on GitHub, joining Cursor and GitHub Copilot in publishing formal specifications for third-party integrations.

title: The Top-Ranked Open-Source AI Memory System Is Now Free
summary: MemPalace, which claims the best benchmark results among open-source AI memory systems, is available at no cost.

title: A Universal Prediction Engine Uses Swarm Intelligence to Forecast Anything
summary: MiroFish is a new open-source engine that applies swarm intelligence — modeled on how bird flocks or ant colonies make collective decisions — to prediction tasks across any domain.

title: Astro Releases a Sandbox Framework for Running AI Agents Safely
summary: Flue, from the team behind the Astro web framework, is a sandboxed environment for running AI agents in isolation so they cannot accidentally affect systems they should not touch.

title: CopilotKit Proposes a Universal Protocol for AI Agent Interfaces
summary: CopilotKit — a React and Angular library for building AI-powered interfaces — launched the AG-UI Protocol, a proposed standard defining how AI agents communicate with front-end applications.

title: Microsoft Open-Sources a Frontier Voice AI Model
summary: Microsoft released VibeVoice on GitHub — a free, open-source voice AI model built to generate natural-sounding speech at a quality level usually reserved for paid, closed systems.

title: A Free Blueprint for Running Your Own Personal AI Setup
summary: Developer danielmiessler released Personal AI Infrastructure, an open-source framework for organizing AI agents and tools around your own life and work instead of a single company's app.

title: A Free AI System Automates Your Entire Job Search
summary: Developer santifer released Career Ops, a free tool built on Claude Code that handles tasks like tailoring resumes, generating PDFs, and tracking applications through a visual dashboard — all powered by 14 specialized AI skill modules.

title: A New Framework Teaches AI Coding Agents Better Work Habits
summary: Developer obra published Superpowers, a free framework that packages proven software development practices into reusable 'skills' that AI coding agents can follow.

title: Microsoft Builds a Stronger Sandbox for Running AI Agents
summary: Microsoft released mxc, an open-source system that isolates and contains software — including AI agents — using layered, policy-based rules that define exactly what each program is allowed to touch.

title: A New Offline AI Computer Wants to Keep You Informed When the Internet Doesn't
summary: A developer released Project N.

title: An AI Skill That Teaches Other AI Tools 'Good Taste'
summary: A developer released Taste-Skill, a small add-on you can drop into AI coding tools to stop them from churning out bland, generic-looking results.

title: The Quiet Engine Behind Most Local AI Chatbots Is Trending Again
summary: llama.

title: A New Desktop App Turns Your Notes Into a Personal Knowledge Base
summary: Tolaria is a new desktop application for organizing markdown notes into a connected knowledge base — the kind of system researchers and writers use to link related ideas together over time.

title: A Free Tool Shows How Much a Phone Number Can Reveal About You
summary: GhostTrack is an open-source tool that demonstrates how publicly available information can be pieced together to trace a phone number or general location.

title: Microsoft Builds Durable Workflows Directly Into PostgreSQL
summary: Microsoft published pg_durable, an open-source extension that lets the popular PostgreSQL database track long-running workflows on its own — so if a process is interrupted partway through, it can pick up exactly where it left off instead of restarting from scratch or losing data.

title: A New Rust-Based Search Index Aims to Make AI Search Faster
summary: Developer Ryan Codrai released Turbovec, an open-source vector index — the kind of system AI search tools use to quickly find related pieces of information — built in Rust on top of a project called TurboQuant, with ready-to-use Python bindings.

title: Google Publishes Official AI Agent Skills for Its Own Products
summary: Google released a public repository of agent skills — pre-built instructions that let AI agents understand and work with Google products like Docs, Sheets, Gmail, and Drive without custom setup.

title: 100+ AI Skills for Product Managers, Free to Download
summary: A new open-source collection called PM Skills packs over 100 reusable AI instructions for every phase of product work — from early discovery through launch and growth.

title: A Free Tool Tells You Which AI Model Runs Best on Your Hardware
summary: A command-line tool called whichllm benchmarks local AI models against your actual hardware and ranks them by real performance — not just model size.

title: Goose: An Open-Source AI Agent That Can Actually Run Your Computer
summary: Goose is a free AI agent that goes well beyond suggesting code — it can install software, run tests, edit files, and execute tasks on your machine, all from a single interface.

title: A Visual Guide to Claude Code With Copy-Paste Templates
summary: Developer luongnv89 published claude-howto, a free repository of visual examples and ready-to-use templates for Claude Code — Anthropic's AI coding assistant.

title: Roboflow Supervision: A Free Reusable Toolkit for AI Computer Vision
summary: Roboflow's supervision library — a free, reusable set of computer vision building blocks — is trending again on GitHub.

title: A GitHub Repository Reveals the Hidden Instructions Behind Today's Top AI Tools
summary: A widely shared GitHub repository has compiled the internal 'system prompts' — the detailed instructions that control tone, behavior, and limits — for more than 20 popular AI tools, including Cursor, Replit, Lovable, Devin AI, Windsurf, and Claude Code.

title: A Google Engineer Releases a Free Library of 'Skills' for AI Coding Agents
summary: Addy Osmani, a well-known voice on web development at Google, published a free collection of production-grade 'skills' — reusable instruction sets that teach AI coding agents established engineering practices.

title: An Open-Source AI Toolkit for Healthcare Is Trending on GitHub
summary: OpenMed is a free, open-source project focused on applying AI to healthcare tasks.

title: A New Open-Source Tool Turns Your Wi-Fi Signal Into a Motion Detector
summary: ESPectre is a free tool that detects movement in a room by analyzing subtle changes in your Wi-Fi signal — a technique called CSI, or channel state information — and connects directly to Home Assistant, the popular smart-home platform.

title: OpenCV, the Library Behind Most AI Vision Tools, Is Trending Again
summary: OpenCV — a free, open-source library for computer vision that's been a foundation of image and video processing since 1999 — is back on GitHub's trending list.

title: A Free Tool Can Search 3,000+ Websites for Your Username in Seconds
summary: Maigret, a free open-source tool, searches more than 3,000 websites for a single username and compiles everything it finds — social media accounts, forum profiles, old projects — into one report.

title: Apple Releases Its Own Tool for Running Linux Software on a Mac
summary: Apple published Container, a free open-source tool that lets Mac users run Linux-based software in lightweight virtual machines, built specifically for Apple Silicon chips.

title: A New Project Wants to Give All Your AI Agents One Shared Memory
summary: Hivemind, described by its creators as 'one brain for all your agents,' is a new open-source project aimed at letting multiple AI agents share context and memory instead of each starting from scratch.

title: Your Wi-Fi Router Could Soon Watch Over a Room — Without a Camera
summary: RuView is an open-source project that turns ordinary Wi-Fi signals into a way to detect movement, monitor vital signs, and sense who's in a room — all without recording video.

title: A Popular Tool for Mass-Producing AI Videos Is Trending Again
summary: MoneyPrinterTurbo, an open-source tool that turns a topic or script into a finished short video — voiceover, visuals, and captions included — is back on GitHub's trending list.

title: A Free Step-by-Step Guide to Building an AI Model From Scratch
summary: Developer Fareed Khan published a free, open-source guide that walks through every stage of training a large language model — the kind of technology behind tools like Claude and ChatGPT — from gathering and cleaning training data to generating text.

title: NVIDIA Releases a Security Scanner for AI Agent 'Skills'
summary: NVIDIA published SkillSpector, a free open-source scanner that checks the add-on 'skills' people are increasingly installing into AI agents and coding assistants — looking for malicious code, security vulnerabilities, and requests for more access than a skill should need.

title: A Free Bundle of AI 'Employees' Covers an Entire Small Business
summary: Agency Agents is a free, open-source collection of AI assistants, each tuned for a specific role — from writing website code to running social media accounts.

title: A Long-Trusted Backup Tool Is Trending on GitHub Again
summary: Restic, a free open-source backup program, is back on GitHub's trending list.

title: A Free Alternative to Zendesk and Intercom Is Trending on GitHub
summary: Chatwoot is an open-source customer support platform that combines live chat, email, and other messaging channels into one inbox.

title: An Open-Source Framework Lets AI Systems Improve Themselves Over Time
summary: SIA (Self Improving AI) is a free framework that lets an AI model or agent automatically refine how it performs a task, without someone manually retraining it.

title: A New Dashboard Tracks What Your AI Coding Agents Are Actually Doing
summary: AgentsView is a free, local-first analytics tool that records and visualizes sessions from AI coding agents — including Claude Code, Codex, and more than 20 others — so you can see what each one did, how long it took, and what it cost.
